lines.text: Many learners say: He has the costume of reading at night.
Better: He has the habit of reading at night.
A costume is for a party.
The second! He has the habit of reading at night.

data.wrong: He has the costume of reading at night.
data.right: He has the habit of reading at night.
data.why: A costume is for a party.
data.memory: A habit is what you do often.

quiz.stem: He has the ___ of reading at night.

native.tip: Em português “costume” é o que fazemos sempre; em inglês, isso é “habit.” “Costume” é uma fantasia.
native.caption: Você também diz isso? “He has the costume of reading at night.” 😅 O certo é “He has the habit of reading at night.” Em português “costume” é o que fazemos sempre; em inglês, isso é “habit.” “Costume” é uma fantasia. Ouça a Ama e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “habit”. Agora escreva uma frase sua com “I have the habit of” e treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: In Portuguese “costume” is what we always do; in English, that is a “habit.” A “costume” is for a party.
en.caption: Do you say this too? “He has the costume of reading at night.” 😅 The right way is “He has the habit of reading at night.” In Portuguese “costume” is what we always do; in English, that is a “habit.” A “costume” is for a party. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
